diagnosis: Repeated passive waiting/no-op behavior is overrepresented in candidate/bad runs.
expected_mechanism: A bounded wait budget prevents unproductive polling loops and forces a state-changing recovery action or termination. Expected benefit: fewer repeated operations and faster progress. Cost: premature recovery on genuinely slow interfaces and extra state bookkeeping.
policy_text: Track consecutive waits or no-ops for each unchanged observable state. After two, do not wait again: inspect once, then choose a state-changing alternative, recover, or stop with the blocker. Reset the counter only when new evidence or state change appears.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.value, .stack_frames[3]] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '$2=="strategy:wait"{if($1>0)p+=$1;else n+=-$1} END{printf "candidate=%d base=%d net=%+d ratio=%.2f\n",p,n,p-n,p/n}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Wait operations total 505 on the candidate/bad side versus 122 on the base/good side: +383 excess and 4.14× as many.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[3]=="strategy:wait") | [.value,.stack_frames[2]] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{p+=($1>0?$1:0);n+=($1<0?-$1:0);a[$2]+=$1} END{printf "candidate=%d base=%d net=%+d action_noop_net=%+d\n",p,n,p-n,a["action:noop"]}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Every wait is an action:noop; its signed excess is likewise +383.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[3]=="strategy:wait") | [.value,.stack_frames[0]] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '$2=="result:repeated"{if($1>0)p+=$1;else n+=-$1} END{printf "candidate=%d base=%d net=%+d\n",p,n,p-n}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Wait/no-op operations marked result:repeated total 441 candidate/bad versus 85 base/good, a +356 excess and 5.19× ratio.
